- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 1.00 extremes, model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.00/1.00), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% asymmetric adjustment toward recent sentiment direction.
